hook.text: Darwin kept detailed notebooks about his own thinking process. His metacognitive habit shaped scientific history.

buildup.text: A learning journal records what you studied, what confused you, what clicked, and what you'll try next.

discovery.text: Writing forces precision. Vague feelings of 'that was hard' become specific insights about what exactly was hard.

twist.text: Journals work best when brief and consistent. A three-sentence entry daily beats a long essay monthly.

climax.text: After each session write: what I learned, what confused me, what I'll do differently. Three lines are enough.

punchline.text: Three lines daily. Your learning accelerates.

quiz.question: Why does writing a learning journal improve metacognition?
options: It creates a study guide for future exams
Writing forces vague feelings into specific insights
It replaces the need for self-testing
